title: حِكَايَةُ نُورِ الدِّينِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْفَضْلِ وَأَنِيسِ الْجَلِيسِ
titleEn: The Tale of the Two Viziers and Anīs al-Jalīs, continued
part: Night 35 · The Two Viziers and Anīs al-Jalīs, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 284–296 (Night 35, continuing directly from nights-34), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 35 continues the tale of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī and Anīs al-Jalīs. The vizier al-Faḍl forgives his son and makes him swear never to sell or wed against the slave-girl, then dies; Nūr al-Dīn squanders his inheritance on false friends until he is penniless, and the ten friends shut their doors on him. At Anīs al-Jalīs's urging he takes her to the slave-market, where his father's enemy al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī bids for her; Nūr al-Dīn beats the vizier in the street, the vizier complains to the sultan, and the sultan sends forty swordsmen to seize them. The chamberlain ʿAlam al-Dīn Sinjar warns them, and they flee by ship toward Baghdad. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْخَامِسَةُ وَالثَّلَٰثُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-khāmisatu wa-al-thalāthūna
sentences.l: And when the night, the fifth and the thirty, came to be,
sentences.i: When the thirty-fifth night came,
sentences.n: As on the previous night, the print has الثلثون without the alif of ثلاثون; it is vocalised as it stands, with the dagger alif marking the missing long ā.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْوَزِيرَ قَالَ لِزَوْجَتِهِ إِنَّمَا تَعْلَمِينَ أَنَّ وَرَاءَنَا هَذَا الْعِلْ وَالَّذِي يُقَالُ لَهُ الْمُعِينُ ابْنُ سَاوِى
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-wazīra qāla li-zawjatihi innamā taʿlamīna anna warāʾanā hādhā al-ʿil wa-alladhī yuqālu lahu al-Muʿīnu ibnu Sāwī
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king, the happy one, that the vizier said to his wife: Only (this): you know that behind us (is) this al-ʿil — and the-one-who it-is-said to-him al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwī
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the vizier said to his wife: "You know well that behind us stands that wretch they call al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī;
sentences.n: The speaker is Shahrazād, resuming the tale of the two viziers. The print has العل والذي, which looks corrupt: العل is most likely العلج (ʿilj, “brute, churl”, an abusive word for a foreigner or lout) with its last letter dropped, and the و may be a stray stroke or may be the start of a relative clause; I vocalise العل as it stands and read والذي as “the one who”. The vizier names his rival, whom the earlier part of the tale introduced as al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī; the print's final ى is read as the name's -ī. The sentence runs on into the next unit, and the vizier's speech with it.

sentences.t: وَمَتَي سَمِعَ بِهَذَا الْأَمْرِ تَقَدَّمَ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ وَقَالَ لَهُ وَزِيرُكَ الَّذِي تَزْعُمُ أَنَّهُ يُحِبُّكَ أَخَذَ مِنْكَ عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ وَاشْتَرَى بِهَا جَارِيَةً مَا رَأَى أَحَدٌ مِثْلَهَا فَلَمَّا أَعْجَبَتْهُ قَالَ لِابْنِهِ خُذْهَا أَنْتَ أَحَقُّ بِهَا مِنَ السُّلْطَانِ فَأَخَذَهَا وَأَزَالَ بَكَارَتَهَا وَهَا هِيَ الْجَارِيَةُ عِنْدَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-matā samiʿa bi-hādhā al-amri taqaddama ilā al-sulṭāni wa-qāla lahu wazīruka alladhī tazʿumu annahu yuḥibbuka akhadha minka ʿashara ālāfi dīnārin wa-ishtarā bihā jāriyatan mā raʾā aḥadun mithlahā fa-lammā aʿjabathu qāla li-ibnihi khudhhā anta aḥaqqu bihā mina al-sulṭāni fa-akhadhahā wa-azāla bakāratahā wa-hā hiya al-jāriyatu ʿindahu
sentences.l: And when he hears of this matter, he will come forward to the sultan and say to him: Your vizier, whom you claim loves you, took from you ten thousand dinars and bought with them a slave-girl, not (has) anyone seen her like; and when she pleased him, he said to his son: Take her, you (are) more-deserving of her than the sultan; so he took her and removed her virginity — and lo, she (is) the slave-girl, with him.
sentences.i: and when he hears of this matter, he will go to the sultan and say to him: 'Your vizier, who you imagine loves you, took ten thousand dinars from you and bought with them a slave-girl the like of whom no one has seen. And when she pleased him, he said to his son, "Take her; you have more right to her than the sultan." So he took her and deflowered her, and there she is, in his house.'
sentences.n: The vizier is imagining what his enemy will tell the sultan, so the verbs are in the present (“he hears”, “he says”) as a vivid future; the same chain of present-tense verbs carries through the next unit. The print has متي for متى, with a dotted yā'; I keep the letter as printed. The print gives فأخذها with a precomposed hamza, so that one word keeps it. The story's earlier telling is that the sultan's vizier bought Anīs al-Jalīs for the king with the king's own money and then gave her to his son.

sentences.t: فَيَقُولُ الْمَلِكُ تَكْذِبُ فَيَقُولُ هُوَ لِلْمَلِكِ عَنْ إِذْنِكَ أَهْجُمْ عَلَيْهِ وَآتِيكَ بِهَا فَيَرْسُمُ لَهُ بِذَلِكَ فَيَكْبِسُ الدَّارَ وَيَأْخُذُ الْجَارِيَةَ وَيُحْضِرُهَا لِلسُّلْطَانِ ثُمَّ يَسْأَلُهَا فَمَا تَقْدِرُ تُنْكِرُ
sentences.tr: fa-yaqūlu al-maliku takdhibu fa-yaqūlu huwa li-al-maliki ʿan idhnika ahjum ʿalayhi wa-ātīka bihā fa-yarsumu lahu bi-dhālika fa-yakbisu al-dāra wa-yakhudhu al-jāriyata wa-yuḥḍiruhā li-al-sulṭāni thumma yasʾaluhā fa-mā taqdiru tunkiru
sentences.l: And the king says: You lie; and he says, he, to the king: With your permission, let-me-rush upon him and bring-you her; and he decrees to him that; and he bursts-into the house and takes the slave-girl and brings-her to the sultan, then asks her, and not she-is-able, she-denies.
sentences.i: Then the king says, "You lie." And he says to the king, "With your leave, let me fall upon him and bring her to you." So the king gives him the order, and he raids the house, takes the girl, brings her before the sultan and questions her, and she cannot deny it.
sentences.n: The long chain of present-tense verbs is the vizier's mental picture of what will happen. أهجم and وآتيك are vocalised as plain statements of intent; Classical would put the first in the jussive after the request and the second in the subjunctive, and the print has no way of showing which. فما تقدر تنكر puts a second verb straight after the first without أن (“is not able to deny”), a very common colloquial pattern in the text.

sentences.t: فَيَقُولُ لَهُ يَاسَيِّدِي تَعْلَمُ أَنِّي نَاصِحٌ لَكَ وَلَكِنْ مَالِي عِنْدَكُمْ حَظٌّ فَيُمَثِّلُ بِي السُّلْطَانُ وَالنَّاسُ كُلُّهُمْ يَتَفَرَّجُونَ عَلَيَّ فَتَرُوحُ رُوحِي
sentences.tr: fa-yaqūlu lahu yāsayyidī taʿlamu annī nāṣiḥun laka wa-lākin mālī ʿindakum ḥaẓẓun fa-yumaththilu bī al-sulṭānu wa-al-nāsu kulluhum yatafarrajūna ʿalayya fa-tarūḥu rūḥī
sentences.l: And he says to him: O-my-master, you know that I (am) a sincere-counsellor to you, but what-to-me with you (is) a portion; and the sultan makes-an-example with me, and the people, all-of-them, look-on at me, and goes-off my soul.
sentences.i: Then he says to him, "My lord, you know that I am a sincere adviser to you, but I have no good fortune with you; and so the sultan will make an example of me while all the people look on, and my soul will depart."
sentences.n: The print does not say who is speaking: the “he” who says يا سيدي could be the vizier rehearsing what he fears, and his words slip from the picture of the enemy's report into his own first-person plaint. I translate what is there. مالي عندكم حظ, literally “what is to me with you a portion”, means “I have no standing/luck with you”. مثّل بـ means to mutilate or make an example of someone by a public punishment. يا سيدي is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ زَوْجَتُهُ لَاتُعْلِمْ أَحَدًا وَهَذَا الْأَمْرُ حَصَلَ خُفْيَةً وَسَلِّمْ أَمْرَكَ إِلَى اللَّهِ فِي هَذِهِ الْقَضِيَّةِ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ سَكَنَ قَلْبُ الْوَزِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu zawjatuhu lā-tuʿlim aḥadan wa-hādhā al-amru ḥaṣala khufyatan wa-sallim amraka ilā Allāhi fī hādhihi al-qaḍiyyati fa-ʿinda dhālika sakana qalbu al-wazīri
sentences.l: And she said to him, his wife: Do-not-inform anyone, and this matter happened in-secret, and hand-over your affair to God in this case. And at that the heart of-the-vizier grew-still.
sentences.i: His wife said to him, "Tell no one. This business happened in secret, so commit your affair to God in this matter." At that the vizier's heart was calmed.
sentences.n: لاتعلم is printed as one word; it is read as لا تُعْلِمْ, “do not inform” (the vizier is to tell no one), not لا تَعْلَمُ, “you do not know”. خفية is an adverbial accusative, “secretly”.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْوَزِيرِ وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ نُورِ الدِّينِ عَلِيٍّ فَخَافَ عَاقِبَةَ الْأَمْرِ فَبَقِيَ طُولَ نَهَارِهِ فِي الْبَسَاتِينِ وَيَأْتِي آخِرَ اللَّيْلِ لِأُمِّهِ فَيَنَامُ عِنْدَهَا وَيَقُومُ قَبْلَ الصُّبْحِ وَيَرُوحُ إِلَى الْبُسْتَانِ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ كَذَلِكَ شَهْرًا لَايُرَى وَجْهُهُ لِأَبِيهِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri al-wazīri wa-ammā mā kāna min amri Nūri al-Dīni ʿAliyyin fa-khāfa ʿāqibata al-amri fa-baqiya ṭūla nahārihi fī al-basātīni wa-yaʾtī ākhira al-layli li-ummihi fa-yanāmu ʿindahā wa-yaqūmu qabla al-ṣubḥi wa-yarūḥu ilā al-bustāni wa-lam yazal ka-dhālika shahran lā-yurā wajhuhu li-abīhi
sentences.l: This (is) what was of the affair of the vizier; and as-for what was of the affair of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī: he feared the outcome of the matter, and stayed the length of his day in the gardens, and comes (at) the end of the night to his mother and sleeps with her and rises before the morning and goes off to the garden; and he did not cease thus a month, not seen his face by his father.
sentences.i: So much for the vizier. As for Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, he feared how the matter would end, and spent the whole day in the gardens, coming to his mother at the end of the night, sleeping beside her, rising before dawn and going off to the garden; and he went on so for a month, his face never seen by his father.
sentences.n: هذا ما كان من أمر فلان … وأما ما كان من أمر فلان is the story-teller's stock formula for turning from one party to the other (“this was what happened to X; as for Y…”). The verbs change from past to present (ويأتي، فينام، ويقوم، ويروح) to describe his habit. لايرى is printed as one word and is read as passive, لا يُرَى وجهه لأبيه, “his face is not seen by his father”; the active reading “he does not show his face” is possible too.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ أُمُّهُ لِأَبِيهِ يَا سَيِّدِي هَلْ نَعْدَمُ الْجَارِيَةَ وَنَعْدَمُ الْوَلَدَ فَإِنْ طَالَ هَذَا الْأَمْرُ عَلَى الْوَلَدِ هَجَّ مِنَّا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat ummuhu li-abīhi yā sayyidī hal naʿdamu al-jāriyata wa-naʿdamu al-walada fa-in ṭāla hādhā al-amru ʿalā al-waladi hajja minnā
sentences.l: And said his mother to his father: O my master, shall we be-bereft of the slave-girl and be-bereft of the boy? For if this matter lasts long for the boy, he bolts from us.
sentences.i: Then his mother said to his father, "My lord, shall we lose the girl and lose the boy too? For if this goes on much longer, the boy will bolt from us."
sentences.n: هجّ is one of the few prose words the print marks, with a shadda; the vocalisation keeps it. It is a colloquial verb, “to bolt, run off”.

sentences.t: قَالَ لَهَا وَكَيْفَ الْعَمَلُ قَالَتْ لَهُ اِسْهَرْ هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَمْسِكْهُ وَاصْطَلِحْ أَنْتَ وَإِيَّاهُ وَأَعْطِهِ الْجَارِيَةَ فَهِيَ تُحِبُّهُ وَهُوَ يُحِبُّهَا وَأَنَا أُعْطِيكَ ثَمَنَهَا
sentences.tr: qāla lahā wa-kayfa al-ʿamalu qālat lahu ishar hādhihi al-laylata fa-idhā jāʾa amsik-hu wa-iṣṭaliḥ anta wa-iyyāhu wa-aʿṭi-hi al-jāriyata fa-hiya tuḥibbuhu wa-huwa yuḥibbuhā wa-anā uʿṭīka thamanahā
sentences.l: He said to her: And how (is) the doing? She said to him: Stay-awake this night, and when he comes, seize-him, and make-peace, you and he, and give-him the slave-girl, for she loves him and he loves her, and I give-you her price.
sentences.i: He said to her, "And what is to be done?" She said to him, "Keep watch tonight, and when he comes, seize him and make peace with him, you and he, and give him the girl, for she loves him and he loves her; and I will give you her price."
sentences.n: The imperatives are vocalised as commands (اسهر، أمسكه، اصطلح، وأعطه); the print does not mark them, and the sense of the wife's plan is clear. أنا أعطيك ثمنها is a plain present: “I give you her price”, meaning she will make good the ten thousand dinars.

sentences.t: فَصَبَرَ الْوَزِيرُ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ فَلَمَّا أَتَى وَلَدُهُ أَمْسَكَهُ وَأَرَادَ نَحْرَهُ فَأَدْرَكَتْهُ أُمُّهُ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَيْشْ تُرِيدُ تَفْعَلُ مَعَهُ فَقَالَ لَهَا أَذْبَحُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣabara al-wazīru ilā al-layli fa-lammā atā waladuhu amsakahu wa-arāda naḥrahu fa-adrakathu ummuhu wa-qālat lahu ayshin turīdu tafʿalu maʿahu fa-qāla lahā adhbaḥuhu
sentences.l: And the vizier waited until the night; and when his son came, he seized him and wanted his throat-cutting; and his mother overtook him and said to him: What do-you-want, you-do with him? And he said to her: I-slaughter-him.
sentences.i: So the vizier waited until night, and when his son came, he seized him and meant to cut his throat. But the boy's mother caught up with him and said, "What do you mean to do with him?" He said to her, "I will slaughter him!"
sentences.n: ايش is the colloquial contraction of أيّ شيء, “what?”, and تريد تفعل strings two verbs together with no أن, both typical of the spoken language the print lets through. The sukūn on the shīn follows the usual pronunciation of the contraction. اذبحه is read as the first-person answer أذبحه, “I will slaughter him”, to her question.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَلَدُ لِأَبِيهِ هَلْ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْكَ فَتَغَرْ غَرَتْ عَيْنَاهُ بِالدُّمُوعِ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا وَلَدِي كَيْفَ هَانَ عَلَيْكَ ذَهَابُ مَالِي وَرُوحِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-waladu li-abīhi hal ahwanu ʿalayka fa-taghar gharat ʿaynāhu bi-al-dumūʿi wa-qāla lahu yā waladī kayfa hāna ʿalayka dhahābu mālī wa-rūḥī
sentences.l: And the boy said to his father: Am I easier upon you? — and his two eyes welled (with) the tears, and he said to him: O my son, how was-light upon you the going of my wealth and my soul?
sentences.i: Then the boy said to his father, "Am I of so little account to you?" The father's eyes welled with tears, and he said to him, "My son, how could the loss of my wealth and my life seem light to you?"
sentences.n: فتغر غرت is one verb, تغرغرت, “(the eyes) welled up, filled with tears”, which the print splits in two; the pieces are vocalised separately and read together. The eyes are the father's: the subject is the same man who then speaks. هل أهون عليك, “am I easier upon you?”, is a way of asking “do I count for so little to you (that you would kill me)?”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الصَّبِيُّ اِسْمَعْ يَا وَالِدِي مَا قَالَ الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ṣabiyyu ismaʿ yā wālidī mā qāla al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: And the lad said: Hear, O my father, what the poet said.
sentences.i: Then the boy said, "Listen, father, to what the poet said:"

sentences.t:
هَبْنِي جَنَيْتُ فَلَمْ يَزَلْ أَهْلُ النُّهَى * يَهَبُونَ لِلْجَانِي سَمَاحًا شَامِلَا
مَا ذَاعَسَى يَرْجُو عَدُوُّكَ وَهْوَفِي * دَرْكِ الْحَضِيضِ وَأَنْتَ أَعْلَى مَنْزِلَا
sentences.tr:
habnī janaytu fa-lam yazal ahlu al-nuhā * yahabūna li-al-jānī samāḥan shāmilā
mā dhāʿasā yarjū ʿaduwwuka wa-hwafī * darki al-ḥaḍīḍi wa-anta aʿlā manzilā
sentences.l:
Reckon-me (to have) offended — and they have not ceased, the people of-prudence, * to-bestow on-the-offender a pardon, all-embracing.
What perhaps hopes your-enemy, he being in * the-bottom of-the-abyss, while-you (are) higher (in) station?
sentences.i:
Suppose I have offended: the people of understanding have never ceased * to grant the offender a full pardon.
What can your enemy hope for, lying in * the lowest pit, while you stand on the loftiest height?
sentences.n: Verse, copied as pointed in the print (every word is marked there, so nothing is added). The print runs ماذا عسى together as ذاعسى (with ما apart) and وهو في as وهوفي, joining a word to the next. The final -ā of شاملا and منزلا is the rhyme-vowel; شاملا is printed without tanwīn, which I leave as printed. هبني is the imperative “reckon me, suppose me”. The father is being asked to pardon him, and the son's argument is that the powerful forgive, and that an enemy brought low has nothing to hope for.

sentences.t: قَالَ فَعِنْدَ ذَٰلِكَ قَامَ الْوَزِيرُ مِنْ عَلَى صَدْرِ وَلَدِهِ فَقَالَ يَا وَلَدِي عَفَوْتُ عَنْكَ وَحَنَّ قَلْبُهُ
sentences.tr: qāla fa-ʿinda dhālika qāma al-wazīru min ʿalā ṣadri waladihi fa-qāla yā waladī ʿafawtu ʿanka wa-ḥanna qalbuhu
sentences.l: He said: And at that, the vizier rose from upon the chest of his son and said: O my son, I have pardoned (from) you; and his heart yearned.
sentences.i: Thereupon the vizier rose from his son's chest and said, "My son, I pardon you," and his heart was moved to pity.
sentences.n: This continues the scene of the previous page, where the vizier has been sitting on his son's chest. من على ("from upon") is a compound preposition, here simply "off". فعند ذلك ("and at that") is a stock transition between episodes.

sentences.t: وَقَامَ الصَّبِيُّ وَقَبَّلَ يَدَ وَالِدِهِ فَقَالَ يَا وَالِدِي لَوْ عَلِمْتُ أَنَّكَ تُنْصِفُ أَنِيسَ الْجَلِيسِ كُنْتُ وَهَبْتُهَا لَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāma al-ṣabiyyu wa-qabbala yada wālidihi fa-qāla yā wālidī law ʿalimtu annaka tunṣifu Anīsa al-Jalīsi kuntu wahabtuhā laka
sentences.l: And the boy rose and kissed the hand of his father and said: O my father, if I had known that you would do-justice-to Anīs al-Jalīs, I had given-her to you.
sentences.i: The lad rose and kissed his father's hand and said, "Father, had I known that you would deal fairly with Anīs al-Jalīs, I would have given her to you."
sentences.n: The logic of this speech is muddled in the print: as written (علمتُ, "I had known") the son speaks, yet the sense seems to be the father's assurance. We vocalise the words as printed and leave the speakers as they stand. لو … كنت وهبتها is the Middle Arabic habit of putting كان + perfect in the apodosis of لو. تنصف أنيس الجليس: the verb أنصف takes its object directly ("treat justly").

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا وَالِدِي كَيْفَ لَا أُنْصِفُهَا قَالَ لَهُ أُوصِيكَ يَا وَلَدِي أَنَّكَ لَا تَتَزَوَّجْ عَلَيْهَا وَلَا تُضَارَّهَا وَلَا تَبِعْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā wālidī kayfa lā unṣifuhā qāla lahu ūṣīka yā waladī annaka lā tatazawwaj ʿalayhā wa-lā tuḍārrahā wa-lā tabiʿhā
sentences.l: And he said: O my father, how not do-justice-to-her? He said to him: I charge you, O my son, that you not marry over her, and not harm her, and not sell her.
sentences.i: "Father," he said, "how should I not deal fairly with her?" Said the vizier, "I charge you, my son, not to take another wife over her, nor to wrong her, nor to sell her."
sentences.n: The three prohibitions after أنك are vocalised as jussives, which is how the print's last verb تبعها (without yā) can only be read: لا تَبِعْها "do not sell her". A Classical writer would put them after أن لا or use the indicative; we keep what the spelling shows. تزوج على فلانة ("marry over so-and-so") means to take a second wife while the first remains.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا وَالِدِي أَنَا أَحْلِفُ لَكَ أَنِّي لَا أَتَزَوَّجُ عَلَيْهَا وَلَا أَبِيعُهَا فَحَلَفَ عَلَى ذَٰلِكَ وَدَخَلَ عَلَى الْجَارِيَةِ فَأَقَامَ مَعَهَا سَنَةً وَأَنْسَى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى الْمَلِكَ قِصَّةَ الْجَارِيَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā wālidī anā aḥlifu laka annī lā atazawwaju ʿalayhā wa-lā abīʿuhā fa-ḥalafa ʿalā dhālika wa-dakhala ʿalā al-jāriyati fa-aqāma maʿahā sanatan wa-ansā Allāhu taʿālā al-malika qiṣṣata al-jāriyati
sentences.l: And he said to him: O my father, I, I swear to you that I shall not marry over her and shall not sell her. So he swore upon that, and entered upon the girl, and stayed with her a year; and God, Exalted, made-forget the king the story of the girl.
sentences.i: "Father," he said, "I swear to you that I will not marry over her, nor ever sell her." So he took the oath, went in to the girl, and lived with her a year, while God Most High made the king forget the tale of the girl.
sentences.n: دخل على ("enter upon") is the usual idiom for a man going in to a woman, here to live with her as her lord. أنسى الله الملك قصة الجارية: the verb أنسى takes two accusatives ("made the king forget the story"), the king being the one for whom the vizier had bought her.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الْمُعِينُ بْنُ سَاوَى فَبَلَغَهُ الْخَبَرُ لَكِنَّهُ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ يَتَكَلَّمُ لِمَنْزِلَةِ الْوَزِيرِ عِنْدَ السُّلْطَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-Muʿīnu ibnu Sāwā fa-balaghahu al-khabaru lākinnahu lam yaqdir yatakallamu li-manzilati al-wazīri ʿinda al-sulṭāni
sentences.l: And as for al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwī, the news reached-him, but-he did not be-able (he) speak, because-of the rank of the vizier with the sultan.
sentences.i: As for al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī, the news reached him, but he could not speak out, because of the vizier's standing with the sultan.
sentences.n: لم يقدر يتكلم puts two verbs side by side with no أن between them ("he was-not-able, he-speak"), a very common Middle Arabic way of joining a modal to its verb; Classical would say لم يقدر أن يتكلم. The name is written ساوى in the print and is pointed here with a final fatḥa (Sāwā), but it is the same al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī met above; the translation gives Sāwī throughout. لمنزلة: لِـ is "because of, on account of".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا مَضَتِ السَّنَةُ عَبَرَ الْوَزِيرُ فَضْلُ الدِّينِ بْنُ خَاقَانَ الْحَمَّامَ وَخَرَجَ وَهُوَ عَرْقَانُ فَضَرَّ بِهِ الْهَوَاءُ فَلَزِمَ الْوِسَادَ وَطَالَ بِهِ السُّهَادُ وَتَسَلْسَلَ بِهِ الضَّعْفُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā maḍati al-sanatu ʿabara al-wazīru Faḍlu al-Dīni ibnu Khāqāna al-ḥammāma wa-kharaja wa-huwa ʿarqānu fa-ḍarra bihi al-hawāʾu fa-lazima al-wisāda wa-ṭāla bihi al-suhādu wa-tasalsala bihi al-ḍaʿfu
sentences.l: And when the year passed, the vizier Faḍl al-Dīn son-of Khāqān went-through the bath-house, and went out and he sweating; and the air harmed him, so he clave to the pillow, and sleeplessness lengthened with-him, and weakness chained-on with-him.
sentences.i: When the year had gone by, the vizier Faḍl al-Dīn ibn Khāqān passed through the bath and came out in a sweat; the air did him harm, and he took to his bed, long sleepless, with weakness creeping ever further upon him.
sentences.n: In the print فضر به is two words; it reads best as فَضَرَّ بِهِ "it harmed him", not a misprint for فضربه. The vizier is here called Faḍl al-Dīn, where elsewhere he is al-Faḍl ibn Khāqān. السهاد is the poetic word for sleeplessness. تسلسل به الضعف ("weakness linked itself to him") is a chain-image: one weakness after another. هو عرقان is a circumstantial clause, "while he was sweating".

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَٰلِكَ نَادَى وَلَدَهُ نُورَ الدِّينِ عَلِيَّ فَحَضَرَ فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا وَلَدِي اِعْلَمْ أَنَّ الرِّزْقَ مَقْسُومٌ وَالْأَجَلَ مَحْتُومٌ وَلَا بُدَّ لِكُلِّ نَسَمَةٍ مِنْ شُرْبِ كَأْسِ الْمَمَاتِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika nādā waladahu Nūra al-Dīni ʿAliyya fa-ḥaḍara fa-qāla lahu yā waladī iʿlam anna al-rizqa maqsūmun wa-al-ajala maḥtūmun wa-lā budda li-kulli nasamatin min shurbi kaʾsi al-mamāti
sentences.l: So at that he called his son Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, and he came; and he said to him: O my son, know that the provision is apportioned and the term decreed, and there is no escape for every soul from drinking the cup of death.
sentences.i: Then he called his son Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, who came, and said, "My son, know that our daily bread is apportioned and our term decreed, and that no soul can escape drinking the cup of death."
sentences.n: The first clause after أن reads الرزقَ … والأجلَ in the accusative, as the particle requires. ʿAlī is vocalised with fatḥa as an indeclinable apposition (نور الدين علي) because the print gives no alif for the accusative ending. The saying is a proverb-like pair: الرزق مقسوم والأجل محتوم, "provision is divided, the term is sealed". The print spells كأس ("cup") with a precomposed hamza, and that is kept.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu anshada yaqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: Then he recited, saying, poetry:
sentences.i: Then he recited these verses:
sentences.n: The final word شعر ("poetry") is the edition's own label announcing the verse that follows; it is read as a noun, shiʿrun. يقول after أنشد ("he recited, saying") is a pleonastic participial-style phrase that introduces speech.

sentences.t:
اَنَا مَيِّتٌ فَجَلَّ مَنْ لَا يَمُوتُ * وَتَحَقَّقْتُ أَنَّنِي سَا مُوتُ
لَيْسَ مَلِكًا يَمُوتُ بِيَدِهِ مُلْكٌ * اِنَّمَا الْمُلْكُ مُلْكُ مَنْ لَا يَمُوتُ
sentences.tr:
anā mayyitun fa-jalla man lā yamūtu * wa-taḥaqqaqtu annanī sā mūtu
laysa malikan yamūtu bi-yadihi mulkun * innamā al-mulku mulku man lā yamūtu
sentences.l:
I am dead; so exalted is he who does not die, * and I have realised that I shall die.
Not a king is he who dies, in his hand a kingdom; * the kingdom is only the kingdom of him who does not die.
sentences.i:
I am as one dead; exalted be He who never dies. * I know it for certain: I shall die.
No king who dies is a king, though a realm be in his hand; * all sovereignty belongs to Him who never dies.
sentences.n: The edition prints سا موتُ with a space, for سأموت (sa-amūtu, "I shall die"); the archive's marks are kept as they stand and the word is read as printed. All verse words here are pointed in the print itself.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ يَا وَلَدِي مَالِي عِنْدَكَ وَصِيَّةٌ إِلَّا تَقْوَى اللَّهِ وَانْظُرْ فِي الْعَوَاقِبِ وَالْوَصِيَّةُ بِالْجَارِيَةِ أَنِيسِ الْجَلِيسِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla yā waladī mālī ʿindaka waṣiyyatun illā taqwā Allāhi wa-unẓur fī al-ʿawāqibi wa-al-waṣiyyatu bi-al-jāriyati Anīsi al-Jalīsi
sentences.l: Then he said: O my son, there is-not-to-me with you a charge except fear of God; and look into the ends; and the charge (is) with-regard-to the girl Anīs al-Jalīs.
sentences.i: Then he said, "My son, I have no charge for you but the fear of God; look to the end of things. And my charge is concerning the girl Anīs al-Jalīs."
sentences.n: مالي is one word in the print; it is read as ما لي ("I have not") followed by عندك. العواقب ("the ends, the outcomes") is the sense of "consider the consequences". والوصية بالجارية is elliptical, with the verb ("I charge you") understood; the noun is left in the nominative as a free-standing topic.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا أَبَتِ وَمَنْ مِثْلُكَ وَقَدْ كُنْتَ مَعْرُوفًا بِفِعْلِ الْخَيْرِ وَالدُّعَاءِ عَلَى الْمَنَابِرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā abati wa-man mithluka wa-qad kunta maʿrūfan bi-fiʿli al-khayri wa-al-duʿāʾi ʿalā al-manābiri
sentences.l: And he said to him: O my father, and who (is) like you, and you had been known for the doing of the good and the prayer upon the pulpits.
sentences.i: "Father," said he, "who is like you? You are known for your good works and for the prayers said for you from the pulpits."
sentences.n: يا أبتِ is the old vocative "O father" with the feminine-looking ending -ati; it is a respectful and affectionate address. والدعاء على المنابر: the Friday sermon prays for rulers and notables, so the phrase says that the vizier was prayed for from the pulpits. وقد كنت … is the circumstantial "when you have been".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا وَلَدِي أَرْجُو مِنَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى الْقَبُولَ ثُمَّ نَطَقَ بِالشَّهَادَتَيْنِ فَكُتِبَ مِنْ أَهْلِ السَّعَادَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā waladī arjū mina Allāhi taʿālā al-qabūla thumma naṭaqa bi-al-shahādatayni fa-kutiba min ahli al-saʿādati
sentences.l: And he said to him: O my son, I hope from God, Exalted, the acceptance; then he uttered the two testimonies, and it was written (of him) among the people of felicity.
sentences.i: "My son," he said, "I hope for acceptance from God Most High." Then he pronounced the two testimonies of faith, and was written down among the people of happiness.
sentences.n: فَكُتِبَ is one of the few prose words the print itself points, with fatḥa on the fā and kāf's damma, kasra and fatḥa; the archive's marks are kept exactly. The change of subject ("it was written") is not marked, and the subject of فكتب is the vizier, now dead. بالشهادتين are the two testimonies, that there is no god but God and that Muḥammad is His messenger.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَٰلِكَ انْقَلَبَ الْقَصْرُ بِالْعِيَاطِ وَانْصَلَ الْخَبَرُ بِالسُّلْطَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika inqalaba al-qaṣru bi-al-ʿiyāṭi wa-inṣala al-khabaru bi-al-sulṭāni
sentences.l: So at that the palace turned-over with the wailing, and the news joined-on with the sultan.
sentences.i: At that the palace was turned upside down with lamentation, and the news reached the sultan.
sentences.n: العياط is the colloquial word for loud wailing, a mark of Egyptian speech. وانصل is vocalised as printed (inṣala); it is probably a slip or dialect form for اتصل (ittaṣala, "it reached"), and is given that sense here.

sentences.t: وَسَمِعَتْ أَهْلُ الْمَدِينَةِ بِوَفَاةِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ خَاقَانَ فَبَكَى عَلَيْهِ الصِّبْيَانُ فِي مَكَاتِبِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-samiʿat ahlu al-madīnati bi-wafāti al-Faḍli ibni Khāqāna fa-bakā ʿalayhi al-ṣibyānu fī makātibihā
sentences.l: And the people of the city heard of the death of al-Faḍl son-of Khāqān, and the boys wept over him in its schools.
sentences.i: The townsfolk heard of the death of al-Faḍl ibn Khāqān, and even the boys in the schools wept for him.
sentences.n: سمعت is feminine singular before the plural-sense noun أهل ("people"), agreeing with the collective; a Classical writer could equally have used the masculine. بوفاة: سمع بـ means "hear of", the verb choosing the preposition.

sentences.t: وَنَهَضَ وَلَدُهُ نُورُ الدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ وَجَهَّزَهُ وَحَضَرَتِ الْأُمَرَاءُ وَالْوُزَرَاءُ وَأَرْبَابُ الدَّوْلَةِ وَأَهْلُ الْمَدِينَةِ وَكَانَ فِيمَنْ حَضَرَ الْجَنَازَةَ الْوَزِيرُ الْمُعِينُ ابْنُ سَاوَى
sentences.tr: wa-nahaḍa waladuhu Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun wa-jahhazahu wa-ḥaḍarati al-umarāʾu wa-al-wuzarāʾu wa-arbābu al-dawlati wa-ahlu al-madīnati wa-kāna fīman ḥaḍara al-janāzata al-wazīru al-Muʿīnu ibnu Sāwā
sentences.l: And his son Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī rose and prepared-him, and there were present the emirs and the viziers and the lords of the state and the people of the city; and among-whom attended the funeral was the vizier al-Muʿīn son-of Sāwī.
sentences.i: His son Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī arose and made him ready for burial. The emirs and viziers, the officers of state and the townsfolk all attended, and among those at the funeral was the vizier al-Muʿīn ibn Sāwī.
sentences.n: جهزه is the usual word for preparing a dead body for burial, washing and shrouding it. أرباب الدولة ("lords of the dynasty/state") are its office-holders. وكان فيمن حضر: كان is singular because the subject, the vizier, follows it.

sentences.t: وَأَنْشَدَ بَعْضُهُمْ عِنْدَ خُرُوجِ جَنَازَتِهِ مِنَ الدَّارِ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-anshada baʿḍuhum ʿinda khurūji janāzatihi mina al-dāri shiʿrun
sentences.l: And some of them recited, at the going-out of his bier from the house, poetry:
sentences.i: As his bier was carried out of the house, one of those present recited these verses:
sentences.n: As above, شعر is the edition's own label for the verse; the pronoun in بعضهم points to the mourners. جنازة can mean both the bier and the funeral procession.

sentences.t:
يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ لَقَدْ فَارَقْتُ اَحْبَابِي * وَغَسَّلُونِي عَلَى لَوْحٍ مِنَ الْبَابِ
وَجَرَّدُونِي ثِيَابًا كُنْتُ لَابِسَهَا * وَاَلْبَسُونِي ثِيَابًا غَيْرَ اَثْوَابِي
وَحَمَّلُونِي عَلَى اَعْنَاقِ اَرْبَعَةٍ * اِلَى الْمُصَلَّى وَبَعْضُ النَّاسِ صَلَّى بِي
صَلَّوْا عَلَيَّ صَلَاةً لَا سُجُودَ لَهَا * صَلَّى عَلَيَّ جَمِيعُ النَّاسِ اَصْحَابِي
وَشَيَّعُونِي اِلَى دَارٍ مُقَنْطَرَةٍ * يَفْنَى الزَّمَانُ وَلَا يُفْتَحُ لَهَا بَابِي
sentences.tr:
yawma al-khamīsi laqad fāraqtu aḥbābī * wa-ghassalūnī ʿalā lawḥin mina al-bābi
wa-jarradūnī thiyāban kuntu lābisahā * wa-albasūnī thiyāban ghayra athwābī
wa-ḥammalūnī ʿalā aʿnāqi arbaʿatin * ilā al-muṣallā wa-baʿḍu al-nāsi ṣallā bī
ṣallaw ʿalayya ṣalātan lā sujūda lahā * ṣallā ʿalayya jamīʿu al-nāsi aṣḥābī
wa-shayyaʿūnī ilā dārin muqanṭaratin * yafnā al-zamānu wa-lā yuftaḥu lahā bābī
sentences.l:
On the day of Thursday I have indeed parted from my loved-ones, * and they washed me upon a plank from the door.
And they stripped me of garments I used to wear, * and clothed me in garments other-than my robes.
And they carried me upon the necks of four * to the place-of-prayer, and some of the people prayed with-me.
They prayed over me a prayer without prostration to it; * over me prayed all the people, my companions.
And they escorted me to a vaulted house; * time perishes and not is-opened for it my door.
sentences.i:
On Thursday I parted from those I loved, * and they washed me on a plank from a door.
They stripped from me the clothes I wore, * and dressed me in garments not my own.
They bore me on the necks of four * to the place of prayer, and some prayed over me.
They prayed over me a prayer without prostration; * all the people prayed over me, my companions.
Then they led me to a vaulted house, * where time passes away and my door is not opened to it.
sentences.n: The first verses of this poem are the well-known lament of the dead man on his own funeral. The prayer for the dead is said standing, without prostration, hence صلاة لا سجود لها. The last line is obscure: ولا يفتح لها بابي ("and my door is not opened for it") may mean that nothing opens the tomb for time, or that the speaker's door will not open again; the word بابي is also the rhyme. All verse words are pointed in the print and are copied as printed.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا وَارَاهُ التُّرَابَ وَرَجَعَتِ الْأَهْلُ وَالْأَصْحَابُ رَجَعَ نُورُ الدِّينِ وَقَدِ انْتَحَبَ مِنَ الْبُكَاءِ وَلِسَانُ الْحَالِ يَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā wārāhu al-turāba wa-rajaʿati al-ahlu wa-al-aṣḥābu rajaʿa Nūru al-Dīni wa-qadi intaḥaba mina al-bukāʾi wa-lisānu al-ḥāli yaqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And when he had covered-him (with) the dust, and the family and the companions had returned, Nūr al-Dīn returned, having sobbed from the weeping, and the tongue of the state saying these verse-lines.
sentences.i: When he had laid his father in the earth, and the household and the friends had gone home, Nūr al-Dīn returned, racked with sobbing, while the tongue of his plight spoke these verses.
sentences.n: The sentence has no named object for وارى; the burial is that of his father (the vizier), as the following lines show. رجعت is feminine singular before the plural subject الاهل والاصحاب, a common pattern when the verb comes first. لسان الحال, “the tongue of the state”, is the stock phrase for what a condition says without speaking it.

sentences.t:
هُمْ رَحَلُوا يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ عَشِيَّةً * فَوَدَّعْتُهُمْ لَمَّا اسْتَقَلُّوا وَدَّعُوا
فَلَمَّا تَوَلَّوْا رَاحَتِ النَّفْسُ مَعَهُمْ * فَقُلْتُ ارْجِعِي قَالَتْ اِلَى اَيْنَ اَرْجِعُ
اِلَى جَسَدٍ مَا فِيهِ رُوحٌ وَلَا دَمٌ * وَمَا فِيهِ اِلَّا عَظْمَةٌ تَتَقَعْقَعُ
وَعَيْنَايَ قَدْ اَعْمَا هُمَا شِدَّةُ الْبُكَا * وَاُذْنِي غَدَتْ صَمَّاءَ مَا لَيْسَ تَسْمَعُ
sentences.tr:
hum raḥalū yawma al-khamīsi ʿashiyyatan * fa-waddaʿtuhum lammā istaqallū waddaʿū
fa-lammā tawallaw rāḥati al-nafsu maʿahum * fa-qultu irjiʿī qālat ilā ayna arjiʿu
ilā jasadin mā fīhi rūḥun wa-lā damun * wa-mā fīhi illā ʿaẓmatun tataqaʿqaʿu
wa-ʿaynāya qad aʿmāhumā shiddatu al-bukā * wa-udhnī ghadat ṣammāʾa mā laysa tasmaʿu
sentences.l:
They, they departed (on the) day (of) Thursday, evening * and I bade-them-farewell when they set-out, they bade farewell.
And when they turned-away, the soul went-off with them * and I said: Return! She said: To where shall I return?
To a body — not in it (is) spirit and not blood * and not in it except a bone (that) rattles.
And my two eyes — has blinded-them-two the intensity of the weeping * and my ear has-become deaf, (it) is-not hearing.
sentences.i: They left on a Thursday evening, and I bade them farewell as they set out, and they bade me farewell. When they were gone my soul went off with them. I said, "Return!" and it said, "Return to where? To a body with neither spirit nor blood in it, nothing but a bone that rattles?" My eyes are blinded by the violence of my weeping, and my ear has grown deaf and hears nothing.

sentences.t: قَالَ ثُمَّ مَكَثَ شَدِيدَ الْحُزْنِ عَلَى وَالِدِهِ مُدَّةً مَدِيدَةً فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ جَالِسٌ فِي بَيْتِ وَالِدِهِ إذْ طَرَقَ الْبَابَ طَارِقٌ فَنَهَضَ نُورُ الدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ وَفَتَحَ الْبَابَ
sentences.tr: qāla thumma makatha shadīda al-ḥuzni ʿalā wālidihi muddatan madīdatan fa-baynamā huwa dhāta yawmin mina al-ayyāmi jālisun fī bayti wālidihi idh ṭaraqa al-bāba ṭāriqun fa-nahaḍa Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun wa-fataḥa al-bāba
sentences.l: He said: Then he stayed, severe-of-the-grief over his father, a period, a long one; and while he, one day of the days, (was) sitting in the house of his father, when a knocker knocked the door, and Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī rose and opened the door.
sentences.i: It is told that he remained in bitter grief for his father a long while. One day, as he sat in his father's house, someone knocked at the door, and Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī rose and opened it.
sentences.n: شديد الحزن is in the accusative as a state (“severe in grief”): he stayed in that condition. بينما … إذ is the usual frame “while he was …, suddenly …”; the pattern recurs throughout the Nights.

sentences.t: وَإذَا بِرَجُلٍ مِنْ نُدَمَاءِ وَالِدِهِ وَأَصْحَابِهِ قَدْ دَخَلَ فَقَبَّلَ يَدَ نُورِ الدِّينِ وَقَالَ يَاسَيِّدِي مَنْ خَلَّفَ مِثْلَكَ مَا مَاتَ وَهَذَا مَصِيرُ سَيِّدِ الْأَوَّلِينَ وَالْآخِرِينَ يَاسَيِّدِي طِبْ نَفْسًا وَدَعِ الْحُزْنَ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-rajulin min nudamāʾi wālidihi wa-aṣḥābihi qad dakhala fa-qabbala yada Nūri al-Dīni wa-qāla yā sayyidī man khallafa mithlaka mā māta wa-hādhā maṣīru sayyidi al-awwalīna wa-al-ākhirīna yā sayyidī ṭib nafsan wa-daʿi al-ḥuzna
sentences.l: And behold, with a man from (the) boon-companions of his father and his companions, who had entered, and he kissed the hand of Nūr al-Dīn and said: O my master, whoever leaves-behind the like of you has-not died; and this (is) the end of the master of the first-ones and the last-ones; O my master, be-good (in) soul and leave the grief.
sentences.i: And lo, a man who had been one of his father's boon companions and friends came in and kissed Nūr al-Dīn's hand, saying, "My lord, he who leaves behind one like you has not died. This is the end that came even to the lord of the first and the last. My lord, take heart and put your grief aside."
sentences.n: وإذا برجل: the بـ after إذا of surprise only marks what appears (“and behold, a man”); the pattern recurs. “The lord of the first and the last” is a title of the Prophet Muḥammad: if even he died, the visitor means, death comes to all. طب نفسا, “be good of soul”, is the idiom for “cheer up”.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ نَهَضَ نُورُ الدِّينِ إلَى الْقَاعَةِ الَّتِي لِلْجُلُوسِ وَنَقَلَ إلَيْهَا مَا يَحْتَاجُهُ وَاجْتَمَعَ عَلَيْهِ أَصْحَابُهُ.
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika nahaḍa Nūru al-Dīni ilā al-qāʿati allatī li-al-julūsi wa-naqala ilayhā mā yaḥtājuhu wa-ijtamaʿa ʿalayhi aṣḥābuhu.
sentences.l: And at that, Nūr al-Dīn rose to the hall which (is) for the sitting, and moved to it what he needed, and his companions gathered upon him.
sentences.i: Then Nūr al-Dīn rose and went to the sitting-hall, had carried there all he needed, and his friends gathered about him.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَ جَارِيَتَهُ وَاجْتَمَعَ عَلَيْهِ عَشَرَةٌ مِنْ أَوْلَادِ التُّجَّارِ ثُمَّ إنَّهُ أَكَلَ الطَّعَامَ وَشَرِبَ الشَّرَابَ وَجَلُدَ مَقَا مَا بَعْدَ مَقَامٍ وَصَارَ يُعْطِي وَيَتَكَرَّمُ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadha jāriyatahu wa-ijtamaʿa ʿalayhi ʿasharatun min awlādi al-tujjāri thumma innahu akala al-ṭaʿāma wa-shariba al-sharāba wa-jaluda maqā mā baʿda maqāmin wa-ṣāra yuʿṭī wa-yatakarramu
sentences.l: And he took his slave-girl, and ten of the sons of the merchants gathered upon him; then he ate the food and drank the drink and persevered (in) a session after a session, and became (one who) gives and acts-generously.
sentences.i: He took his slave-girl with him, and ten merchants' sons gathered about him. He ate and drank, and kept up one session after another, and took to giving freely and spending like a lord.
sentences.n: وجلد is vocalised as printed, jaluda, “was steadfast, held out”, which gives “kept up session after session”; it may be a compositor's slip for وجلس, “and sat”, which would give nearly the same sense. مقا ما is one word, مقاما, “a session”, split by a stray space in the print (the same word is printed whole further on).

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ جَاءَ لَهُ وَكِيلُهُ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَاسَيِّدِي نُورَ الدِّينِ أَمَا سَمِعْتَ قَوْلَ بَعْضِهِمْ مَنْ يُنْفِقْ وَ لَمْ يَحْسِبْ افْتَقَرَ وَلَمْ يَشْعُرْ وَالشَّا عَرِيَقُ—ولُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika jāʾa lahu wakīluhu wa-qāla lahu yā sayyidī Nūra al-Dīni a-mā samiʿta qawla baʿḍihim man yunfiq wa lam yaḥsib iftaqara wa-lam yashʿur wa-al-shā ʿari yaqūlu
sentences.l: And at that, there came to him his steward and said to him: O my master Nūr al-Dīn, have-you-not heard the saying of some of them: Whoever spends and does-not reckon, (he) became-poor, and did-not perceive; and the poet says:
sentences.i: Then his steward came to him and said, "My lord Nūr al-Dīn, have you not heard what one of them has said: 'He who spends without reckoning comes to poverty and never notices it'? And the poet says:
sentences.n: The print breaks the last two words (والشا عريق—ول); they are read as والشاعر يقول, “and the poet says”, and the letters are kept exactly as printed. In من ينفق … افتقر the condition is jussive but the answer is a perfect, “he became poor”, a common Middle Arabic way of stating a general truth.

sentences.t:
اَصُونُ دَرَاهِمِي وَاَذُبُّ عَنْهَا * لِعِلْمِي اَنَّهَا سَيْفِي وَنُرْسِي
اَبْذُلْهَا اِلَى اَعْلَى الْاَعَادِي * وَابْذُلِ فِي الْوَرَى سَعْيِي بِنَفْسِي
فَاَكُلُهَا وَاَشْرِبُهَا هَنِيئاً * وَلَا اَشْكُو اِلَى اَحَدٍ بِفَلْسِ
وَاَحْفَظُ دِرْهَمِي عَنْ كُلِّ شَخْصٍ * لَئِيمِ الطَّبْعِ لَا يَصْفُو لِاِنْسِي
اَحَبُّ اِلَيَّ مِنْ قَوْلِي لِنَذْلٍ * اَنِلْنِي دِرْهَمًا لِغَدٍ بِخَمْسِ
فَيَعْرِضُ وَجْهَهُ وَيَصُدُّ عَنِّي * فَتَبْقَى مِثْلَ نَفْسِ الْكَلْبِ نَفْسِي
فَيَاذُلَّ الرِّجَالِ بِغَيْرِ مَالٍ * وَلَوْكَانَتْ فَضَائِلُهُمْ كَشَمْسِ
sentences.tr:
aṣūnu darāhimī wa-adhubbu ʿanhā * li-ʿilmī annahā sayfī wa-nursī
abdhulhā ilā aʿlā al-aʿādī * wa-abdhuli fī al-warā saʿyī bi-nafsī
fa-akuluhā wa-ashribuhā hanīʾan * wa-lā ashkū ilā aḥadin bi-falsi
wa-aḥfaẓu dirhamī ʿan kulli shakhṣin * laʾīmi al-ṭabʿi lā yaṣfū li-insī
aḥabbu ilayya min qawlī li-nadhlin * anilnī dirhaman li-ghadin bi-khamsi
fa-yaʿriḍu wajhahu wa-yaṣuddu ʿannī * fa-tabqā mithla nafsi al-kalbi nafsī
fa-yā dhulla al-rijāli bi-ghayri mālin * wa-law kānat faḍāʾiluhum ka-shamsi
sentences.l:
I guard my dirhams and ward off (harm) from them * for my knowing that they (are) my sword and my shield.
Shall I lavish them on the highest of the enemies * and spend among creation my striving in my own person?
No — I eat them and drink them, with relish * and do not complain to anyone about a fals.
And I keep my dirham from every person * base-of-nature, (who) is not sincere to a human being.
Dearer to me than my saying to a wretch * Grant me a dirham till tomorrow, for five!
And he turns away his face and shuns me * and my soul remains like the soul of the dog.
So O the abasement of men without wealth * even if their merits were like the sun!
sentences.i: I guard my dirhams and fend off harm from them, knowing they are my sword and my shield. Shall I squander them on the loftiest of foes, and spend my own effort among mankind? No: I eat them and drink them with relish, and never whine to anyone over a copper. I keep my coin from every low-natured fellow who is true to no man. Dearer to me than saying to a wretch, "Lend me a dirham till tomorrow, for five," and having him turn his face and shun me while my spirit pants like a dog's. Alas, the abasement of men without money, though their merits shine like the sun!
sentences.n: The second line is obscure in the print; the rendering takes it as a rhetorical question (“shall I lavish them on my enemies?”), answered by the next line, and may be corrupt. The last words of the sixth line, نفس الكلب نفسي, play on نفس: “the soul/breath of the dog” and “my soul”; the translation lets “pants like a dog's” carry the play.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ يَاسَيِّدِي هَذِهِ النَّفَقَةُ الْجَزِيلَةُ وَالْمَوَاهِبُ الْعَظِيمَةُ تُفْنِى الْمَالَ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla yā sayyidī hādhihi al-nafaqatu al-jazīlatu wa-al-mawāhibu al-ʿaẓīmatu tufnī al-māla
sentences.l: Then he said: O my master, this spending, the abundant, and the gifts, the great, finish-off the wealth.
sentences.i: Then he said, "My lord, this lavish spending and these great gifts will use up your wealth."
sentences.n: The print has تفنى المال; it is read as تُفْنِى, “brings to an end”, with المال as the object: spending and gifts that exhaust the money.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ نُورُ الدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ مِنْ وَكِيلِهِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ نَظَرَ إلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ جَمِيعُ مَا قُلْتَهُ لَا أَسْمَعُ مِنْهُ وَلَا كَلِمَةً فَإنِّي سَمِعْتُ الشَّــاعِرَ يَقُــولُ شِعْـر—ر
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun min wakīlihi hādhā al-kalāma naẓara ilayhi wa-qāla lahu jamīʿu mā qultahu lā asmaʿu minhu wa-lā kalimatan fa-innī samiʿtu al-shāʿira yaqūlu shiʿr—r
sentences.l: And when Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī heard from his steward this speech, he looked at him and said to him: The whole of what you said, I do not hear from it, nor a word; for I heard the poet saying poetry —
sentences.i: When Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī heard these words from his steward he looked at him and said, "Everything you have said, I will not listen to — not a word of it. For I have heard the poet say:"
sentences.n: The line ends in a broken form, شعر—ر, a dash and a stray ر after شعر; it is read as شِعْر, “verse”, and the letters are kept as printed. The edition's stretching-strokes in الشـاعر and يقـول are kept too.

sentences.t:
اِذَا مَا مَلَكْتُ الْمَالَ كَفِّي وَلَمْ اَجُدْ * فَلَا سَلِمَتْ كَفِّي وَلَا نَهَضَتْ رِجْلِي
فَمَا تُوا بَخِيلاً نَالَ مَجْدًا بِبُخْلِهِ * وَهَاتُوا اَرُونِي بَاذِلاً مَاتَ بِالْبَذْلِ
sentences.tr:
idhā mā malaktu al-māla kaffī wa-lam ajud * fa-lā salimat kaffī wa-lā nahaḍat rijlī
fa-mā tū bakhīlan nāla majdan bi-bukhlihi * wa-hātū arūnī bādhilan māta bi-al-badhli
sentences.l:
When I have-taken-possession (of) the wealth, my palm, and have not given * then may my palm not be safe and my foot not rise.
So — bring a miser (who) won glory by his miserliness * and bring, show me a giver (who) died of giving!
sentences.i: If I hold the wealth in my grasp and do not give, may my hand never be safe and my foot never rise. Bring me a miser who won glory by his miserliness, and show me a giver who died of giving!
sentences.n: The first line's grammar is awkward (ملكت المال كفي): it is rendered by its evident sense, “if I hold the wealth in my hand”. In the second line the print has فما توا in two pieces; this looks like a misprint for فهاتوا, “so bring!”, parallel to وهاتوا, and the translation follows that sense. The edition prints the verse pointed, and the pointing is kept as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ اِعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْوَكِيلُ إنِّي أُرِيدُ إذَا فَضَلَ عِنْدَكَ قَدْرُ غَدَائِي أَنْ لَاتُحَمِّلَنِي هَمَّ عَشَائِي
sentences.tr: thumma qāla iʿlam ayyuhā al-wakīlu innī urīdu idhā faḍala ʿindaka qadru ghadāʾī an lā tuḥammilanī hamma ʿashāʾī
sentences.l: Then he said: Know, O steward, that I want — if there remains with you the measure of my lunch — that you not burden me (with) the worry of my supper.
sentences.i: Then he said, "Know, steward, that I ask only this: if enough is left with you for my midday meal, do not burden me with the worry of my supper."

sentences.t: فَوَلَّى مِنْ عِنْدِهِ الْوَكِيلُ إلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِهِ وَأَقْبَلَ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ عَلَى اللَّذَّاتِ فِي أَطْيَبِ عَيْشٍ وَ مَاهُوَ فِيــهِ
sentences.tr: fa-wallā min ʿindihi al-wakīlu ilā ḥāli sabīlihi wa-aqbala Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun ʿalā al-ladhdhāti fī aṭyabi ʿayshin wa mā huwa fīhi
sentences.l: And the steward turned away from his presence to the state of his way, and Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī turned-toward the pleasures, in the sweetest of living and what he (was) in.
sentences.i: The steward withdrew from his presence and went his way, and Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī gave himself up to pleasure, living the sweetest of lives amid all that he had.
sentences.n: إلى حال سبيله, “to the state of his way”, means he went his way.

sentences.t: وَكُلُّ مَنْ يَقُولُ لَهُ مِنْ نُدَمَائِهِ هَذَا الشَّيْ مَلِيحٌ يَقُولُ هُوَلَكَ هِبَةٌ وَيَقُولُ الْآخَرُ يَا سَيِّدِي الدَّارُ الْفُلَانِيَّةُ مَلِيحَةٌ يَقُولُ هِيَ هِبَةٌ لَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-kullu man yaqūlu lahu min nudamāʾihi hādhā al-shay malīḥun yaqūlu huwa laka hibatun wa-yaqūlu al-ākharu yā sayyidī al-dāru al-fulāniyyatu malīḥatun yaqūlu hiya hibatun laka
sentences.l: And every-one who says to him from his boon-companions: This thing (is) fine — he says: It-is to-you a gift; and the other says: O my master, the house, the so-and-so one, (is) fine — he says: It (is) a gift for you.
sentences.i: And whenever one of his companions said to him, "This is a fine thing," he answered, "It is yours, a gift"; and when another said, "My lord, such-and-such a house is lovely," he said, "It is a gift to you."
sentences.n: الشي is the print's spelling of الشيء, “the thing”; the vocalisation leaves the hamza unwritten, as the print does. هولك is the print's single word for هو لك, “it is yours”.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ نُورُالدِّينِ يَعْمَلُ لَهُمْ أَوَّلَ النَّهَارِ مَقَامًا وَفِى آخِرِ النَّهَارِ مَقَامًا إلَى أَنْ مَكَثَ سَنَةً عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ وَبَعْدَ السَّنَةِ فَبَيْنَمَاهُوَ قَاعِدٌ وَإذَا بِالْجَارِيَةِ أَنِيسِ الْجَلِيسِ تُنْشِدُ شِعْرً
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal Nūru al-Dīni yaʿmalu lahum awwala al-nahāri maqāman wa-fī ākhiri al-nahāri maqāman ilā an makatha sanatan ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli wa-baʿda al-sanati fa-baynamā huwa qāʿidun wa-idhā bi-al-jāriyati Anīsi al-Jalīsi tunshidu shiʿran
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn did-not cease making for them, at the first of the day, a session, and at the last of the day, a session, until he stayed a year on this state; and after the year, while he (was) sitting, behold, with the slave-girl Anīs al-Jalīs reciting poetry.
sentences.i: And Nūr al-Dīn went on holding a gathering for them at the start of the day and another at its end, until a year had passed in this fashion. Then one day, as he sat, behold, his slave-girl Anīs al-Jalīs was reciting these lines:
sentences.n: فبينماهو … واذا is the same “while he … behold” frame as before, with the second half opened by واذا; the girl's name is Anīs al-Jalīs, “the Companion of the Sitting”. شعر is printed without the alif of the accusative tanwīn, so it is pointed with a bare fatḥatān.

sentences.t:
اَحْسَنْتَ ظَنَّكَ بِالْاَيَّامِ اِذْ حَسُنَتْ * وَلَمْ تَخَفْ سُوءَ مَايَاْتِي بِهِ الْقَدَرُ
وَسَالَمَتْكَ اللَّيَالِي فَاغْتَرَرْتَ بِهَا * وَعِنْدَ صَفْوِ اللَّيَالِي يَحْدُثُ الْكَدِرُ
sentences.tr:
aḥsanta ẓannaka bi-al-ayyāmi idh ḥasunat * wa-lam takhaf sūʾa mā yaʾtī bihi al-qadaru
wa-sālamatka al-layālī fa-ightarartā bihā * wa-ʿinda ṣafwi al-layālī yaḥduthu al-kadiru
sentences.l:
You thought-well your thinking of the days when they were-fair * and did-not fear the evil of what brings with-it the destiny.
And the nights made-peace-with-you, so you were-deceived by them * and at the clearness of the nights occurs the murk.
sentences.i: You thought well of fortune while she smiled, and feared no ill of what fate may bring. The nights made peace with you and you were taken in; but it is in the clear of the nights that the dregs arise.
sentences.n: The print points مَايَاْتِي with a sukun on the alif where the hamza of يأتي belongs; it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنْ شِعْرِهَا وَإِذَا بِالْبَابِ يُطْرَقُ فَقَامَ نُورُالدِّينِ فَتَبِعَهُ بَعْضُ جُلَسَائِهِ مِنْ غَيْرِأَنْ يَعْلَمَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghat min shiʿrihā wa-idhā bi-al-bābi yuṭraqu fa-qāma Nūru al-Dīni fa-tabiʿahu baʿḍu julasāʾihi min ghayri an yaʿlama bihi
sentences.l: And when she had finished from her poem, and-behold, at-the-door (it is) being-knocked; so Nūr al-Dīn rose, and there followed him one-of his companions, from other-than that he know of him,
sentences.i: And when she had finished her poem, behold, there was a knocking at the door. Nūr al-Dīn rose, and one of his companions followed him without his knowing it,
sentences.n: إذا بـ (idhā bi-) introduces the sudden event: “and behold, at the door, a knocking”. The edition prints نورالدين as one word, which is how it is pointed here, and likewise غيران for غير أن. “Poem” here is the song she had just been singing to the company.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَتَحَ الْبَابَ وَجَدَ وَكِيلَهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلَى مَا الْخَبَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā fataḥa al-bāba wajada wakīlahu fa-qāla lahu Nūru al-Dīni ʿalā mā al-khabaru
sentences.l: And when he opened the door, he found his steward, and Nūr al-Dīn said to him: On what (is) the news?
sentences.i: When he opened the door he found his steward, and Nūr al-Dīn said to him: "What is the news?"
sentences.n: The sentence عَلَى مَا الْخَبَرُ (“on what the news?”) is a verbless question; the Arabic simply sets the three words side by side, “what is the news?”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي الَّذِي كُنْتُ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكَ مِنْهُ قَدْ وَقَعَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu yā sayyidī alladhī kuntu akhāfu ʿalayka minhu qad waqaʿa
sentences.l: And he said to him: O my master, the-thing-which I used-to fear for you from it, indeed it has fallen.
sentences.i: He said: "My lord, the thing I feared for you has happened."
sentences.n: خَافَ عَلَى (“fear for”) names the person in danger and خَافَ مِنْ (“fear of”) the danger; both are used here, so “the thing I feared for you, from it” closes on قَدْ وَقَعَ, “it has already come to pass”.

sentences.t: قَالَ وَكَيْفَ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: qāla wa-kayfa dhālika
sentences.l: He said: And how (is) that?
sentences.i: He asked: "And how is that?"

sentences.t: قَالَ اعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ مَا بَقِيَ تَحْتَ يَدِي شَيٌ يُسَاوِي دِرْهَمًا وَلَا أَقَلَّ وَلَا أَكْثَرَ وَهَذِهِ الدَّفَاتِرُ مَوْجُودَةٌ بِالْمَصْرُوفِ الَّذَىٰ صَرَفْتَهُ وَدَفَاتِرُ أَصْلِ مَالِكَ
sentences.tr: qāla iʿlam annahu mā baqiya taḥta yadī shayun yusāwī dirhaman wa-lā aqalla akthara wa-hādhihi al-dafātiru mawjūdatun bi-al-maṣrūfi alladhā ṣarafta-hu wa-dafātiru aṣli mālika
sentences.l: He said: Know that there has not remained under my hand a-thing (being) worth a dirham, nor less, nor more; and these ledgers (are) present, with the expenditure which you spent, and the ledgers of the principal of your wealth.
sentences.i: He said: "Know that nothing is left in my keeping worth a dirham, or less, or more. Here are the ledgers, with the expenditure you have made, and the ledgers of the principal of your wealth."
sentences.n: The edition prints شي for شيء, with the hamza omitted; it is pointed here as written, and read shayʾ. The Classical idiom would not repeat وَلَا before أَقَلَّ and أَكْثَرَ; the Arabic means “not a dirham’s worth, neither less nor more”. بِالْمَصْرُوفِ is “together with the record of what was spent”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ أَطْرَقَ بِرَأْسِهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ وَقَالَ لَاحَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun hādhā al-kalāma aṭraqa bi-raʾsihi ilā al-arḍi wa-qāla lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Allāhi
sentences.l: And when Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī heard this speech, he bowed with his head to the ground and said: There is no power and no strength save by God.
sentences.i: When Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī heard this he bowed his head to the ground and said: "There is no power and no strength save in God."
sentences.n: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ is the pious formula of resignation in the face of misfortune. The print joins لاحول into one word.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الرَّجُلُ الَّذِي تَبِعَهُ خُفْيَةً خَرَجَ لِيَتَسَلَّلَ عَلَيْهِ مَا قَالَهُ لَهُ الْوَكِيلُ رَجَعَ إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ وَقَالَ لَهُمْ انْظُرُوا أَيْشَ تَعْمَلُونَ فَإِنَّ نُورَالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ أَفْلَسَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-rajulu alladhī tabiʿahu khufyatan kharaja li-yatasallala ʿalayhi mā qālahu lahu al-wakīlu rajaʿa ilā aṣḥābihi wa-qāla lahum unẓurū ayshi taʿmalūna fa-inna Nūra al-Dīni ʿaliyyan aflasa
sentences.l: And when the man who had followed him secretly — he went out in-order-that he slip upon him — heard what the steward had said to him, he returned to his companions and said to them: Look what you are doing, for Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī has gone-bankrupt.
sentences.i: The man who had followed him in secret, having slipped out to listen, heard what the steward told him. He went back to his companions and said to them: "Look to what you are about, for Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī has gone bankrupt!"
sentences.n: The sentence is tangled in the print: خَرَجَ لِيَتَسَلَّلَ عَلَيْهِ (“he went out to slip upon him”, that is, to eavesdrop) is a parenthesis between the man’s hearing and the thing he heard, مَا قَالَهُ لَهُ الْوَكِيلُ. It is pointed as printed. أَيْشَ is the colloquial “what”, shortened from أَيُّ شَيْءٍ.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَجَعَ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلِيٌّ نُورُالدِّينِ تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الْغَمُّ فِي وَجْهِهِ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ نَهَضَ وَاحِدٌ مِنَ النُّدَمَاءِ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ وَنَظَرَ إِلَى نُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيٍّ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَاسَيِّدِي عَسَى أَنْ تَأْذَنَ لِي بِالِانْصِرَافِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā rajaʿa ilayhim ʿAliyyun Nūru al-Dīni tabayyana lahumu al-ghammu fī wajhihi fa-ʿinda dhālika nahaḍa wāḥidun mina al-nudamāʾi ʿalā qadamayhi wa-naẓara ilā Nūri al-Dīni ʿAliyyin wa-qāla lahu yā sayyidī ʿasā an taʾdhana lī bi-al-inṣirāfi
sentences.l: And when ʿAlī Nūr al-Dīn returned to them, the gloom became plain to them in his face. At that one of the boon-companions rose on his two feet and looked at Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī and said to him: O my master, perhaps you will permit me the departure?
sentences.i: When ʿAlī Nūr al-Dīn came back to them, the gloom was plain to see upon his face. Thereupon one of the companions rose to his feet, looked at Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī and said: "My lord, perhaps you will give me leave to depart?"
sentences.n: The print writes the master’s name in the reverse order here, عَلِيٌّ نُورُالدِّينِ; it is the same man. The first of the false friends begins to slip away.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ لِمَاذَا الِانْصِرَافُ الْيَوْمَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun li-mādhā al-inṣirāfu al-yawma
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī said: For-what the departure today?
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī asked: "Why leave today?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ إِنَّ زَوْجَتِي تَلِدُو لَايُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أَتَخَلَّفَ عَنْهَا وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أَذْهَبَ إِلَيْهَا وَأَنْظُرَهَا فَأَذِنَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla inna zawjatī talidū lā yumkinunī an atakhallafa ʿanhā wa-urīdu an adhhaba ilayhā wa-anẓurahā fa-adhina lahu
sentences.l: And he said: Indeed my wife, she gives-birth, (and) it is not possible for me that I stay-away from her, and I want that I go to her and look to her. So he gave-leave to him.
sentences.i: He said: "My wife is in labour and I cannot stay away from her; I wish to go to her and see to her." So he gave him leave.
sentences.n: تَلِدُو: the final و is unexplained in the print. It may be a slip for تَلِدُ (“she is giving birth”, here “is in labour”) or the start of a word cut short; it is pointed as printed. In وَأَنْظُرَهَا the verb continues the subjunctive after أَنْ, “and look to her”.

sentences.t: وَنَهَضَ آخَرُ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي نُورَالدِّينِ أُرِيدُ الْيَوْمَ أَنْ أَحْضُرَ عِنْدَ أَخِي فَإِنَّهُ يُطَاهِرُ وَلَدَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-nahaḍa ākharu wa-qāla lahu yā sayyidī Nūra al-Dīni urīdu al-yawma an aḥḍura ʿinda akhī fa-innahu yuṭāhiru waladahu
sentences.l: And another rose and said to him: O my master Nūr al-Dīn, I want today that I attend at my brother, for he is circumcising his son.
sentences.i: Another rose and said: "My lord Nūr al-Dīn, today I wish to be at my brother’s, for he is circumcising his son."
sentences.n: يُطَاهِرُ is a colloquial verb for the circumcision feast; Classical Arabic would say يُطَهِّرُ. The print has it as a plain form III verb, and it is pointed so.

sentences.t: وَكُلُّ وَاحِدٍ صَارَيَسْتَأْذِنُهُ بِحِيلَةٍ وَيَذْهَبُ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِهِ حَتَّى انْصَرَفُوا كُلُّهُمْ وَبَقِيَ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ وَحْدَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kullu wāḥidin ṣāra yastaʾdhinuhu bi-ḥīlatin wa-yadhhabu ilā ḥāli sabīlihi ḥattā inṣarafū kulluhum wa-baqiya Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun waḥdahu
sentences.l: And every one began asking his leave with a pretext and going to the state of his way, until they had all departed and Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī remained alone.
sentences.i: One after another, each began to ask his leave on some pretext and went his way, until all had gone and Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī was left alone.
sentences.n: The print joins the two verbs of صَارَيَسْتَأْذِنُهُ (“became, asks-his-leave”): صَارَ here means “began”, and it is followed by an unmarked imperfect, a Middle Arabic habit. The edition itself prints the hamza of يستأذنه on its seat, and that is kept.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ دَعَىٰ جَارِيَتَهُ وَقَالَ لَهَا يَا أَنِيسَ الْجَلِيسِ مَا تَنْظُرِينَ مَا حَلَّ بِي وَحَكَى لَهَا مَا قَالَ لَهُ الْوَكِيلُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika daʿā jāriyatahu wa-qāla lahā yā Anīsa al-Jalīsi mā tanẓurīna mā ḥalla bī wa-ḥakā lahā mā qāla lahu al-wakīlu
sentences.l: And at that he called his slave-girl and said to her: O Anīs al-Jalīs, do-you-see what has befallen me? And he related to her what the steward had said to him.
sentences.i: Then he called his slave-girl and said: "Anīs al-Jalīs, do you see what has befallen me?" And he told her what the steward had said to him.
sentences.n: ما تنظرين is read here as a reproachful question, “do you not see?”; the particle ما is the Middle Arabic way of opening such a question. The girl’s name is the title of the tale: Anīs al-Jalīs.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَاسَيِّدِي مِنْ مُنْذُ لَيَالِي هَمَمْتُ أَنْ أَقُولَ لَكَ عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ فَسَمِعْتُكَ تُنْشِدُ وَتَقُولُ شِـــعْـــرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā sayyidī min mundhu layālī hamamtu an aqūla laka ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli fa-samiʿtuka tunshidu wa-taqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: And she said: O my master, since some nights I was minded to say to you about this state, and I heard you reciting and saying: Poetry.
sentences.i: She said: "My lord, for some nights now I have been minded to speak to you of this state of things, but I heard you reciting, and you said:"
sentences.n: The edition prints مِنْ مُنْذُ with both prepositions, “from since”, which simply means “ever since”. The last word is the printed rubric شعر, “verse”, that introduces the lines which follow.

sentences.t:
اِذَا جَادَتِ الدُّنْيَا عَلَيْكَ فَجُدْبِهَا * عَلَى النَّاسِ طُرًّا قَبْلَ اَنْ تَتَفَلَّتِ
فَلَا الْجُودُ يُفْنِيهَا اِذَا هِيَ اَقْبَلَتْ * وَلَا الشُّحُّ يُبْقِيهَا اِذَا هِيَ وَلَّتِ
sentences.tr:
idhā jādati al-dunyā ʿalayka fa-jud bi-hā * ʿalā al-nāsi ṭurran qabla an tatafallati
fa-lā al-jūdu yufnīhā idhā hiya aqbalat * wa-lā al-shuḥḥu yubqīhā idhā hiya wallat
sentences.l: When the world gives-freely toward you, then be-lavish with it upon the people, all-together, before that she slip-away; for neither generosity uses-her-up when she has advanced, nor miserliness keeps-her when she has turned-away.
sentences.i: When the world is generous to you, be generous with it to all men before it slips away; for neither giving wastes it when it comes, nor miserliness keeps it when it goes.
sentences.n: Both lines are copied from the archive as printed. The two words اَنْ and اَقْبَلَتْ are pointed in the print on a bare alif; they are kept as printed and read an and aqbalat. The world (الدُّنْيَا) is feminine, so the pronoun in فَجُدْبِهَا, يُفْنِيهَا and يُبْقِيهَا is “her”; the translation says “it”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُكَ تُنْشِدُ هَذِهِ الْأَ بْيَاتَ سَكَتُّ وَلَمْ أُبْدِلَكَ خِطَابًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿtuka tunshidu hādhihi al-abyāta sakattu wa-lam ubdi-laka khiṭāban
sentences.l: And when I heard-you reciting these the-verses, I fell-silent, and I did not give-out to-you a reply.
sentences.i: When I heard you recite these verses I fell silent, and gave you no answer.
sentences.n: The speaker is Anīs al-Jalīs, still addressing Nūr al-Dīn. The print divides الا بيات (read al-abyāt, “the verses”) and runs ابدلك together; it is read أُبْدِ لَكَ, the jussive of أبدى after لم, with its final yāʾ lost in the run-together spelling. Both oddities are kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِىُّ يَا أَنِيسَ الْجَلِيسِ أَنْتِ تَعْرِفِينَ إِنِّي مَا أَوْهَبْتُ مَالِي إِلَّا عَلَى أَصْحَابِي وَهُمْ خَلَّوْنِي بِلَاشَيٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun yā Anīsa al-Jalīsi anti taʿrifīna innī mā awhabtu mālī illā ʿalā aṣḥābī wa-hum khallawnī bi-lā shayʾin
sentences.l: And he said to-her, Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī: O Anīs al-Jalīs, you know that I did not bestow my wealth except upon my companions, and they, they have left me with-no-thing.
sentences.i: Then Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī said to her, "Anīs al-Jalīs, you know that I spent my wealth on none but my friends, and now they have left me with nothing."
sentences.n: The print has the name as نورالدين على with a final ى, kept as printed. ما أوهبت ... إلا is the “not ... except” of restriction, “only”; أوهب is a rare by-form of وهب, “give”, and is read so here. The last word is printed بلاشيٍ with a tanwīn but no hamza; it is read bi-lā shayʾin, “with nothing”.

sentences.t: وَأَظُنُّهُمْ لَايَتْرُكُونَنِي مِنْ غَيْرِ مُوَاسَاةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-aẓunnuhum lā yatrukūnanī min ghayri muwāsātin
sentences.l: And I suppose-them, they-do-not leave-me without consolation.
sentences.i: And I think they will not leave me without some succour.
sentences.n: لا is printed joined to the verb (لايتركونني) and the two nūns of يتركونني are the plural ending and the nūn that supports -ī. The indicative after لا, “they will not”, is ordinary. مواساة is the help one friend gives another out of his own means.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَنِيسُ الْجَلِيسِ وَاللَّهِ مَا يَنْفَعُونَكَ بِنَافِعَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu Anīsu al-Jalīsi wa-Allāhi mā yanfaʿūnaka bi-nāfiʿatin
sentences.l: And she said to-him, Anīs al-Jalīs: By-God, they will not benefit-you with a benefiting.
sentences.i: Anīs al-Jalīs said to him, "By God, they will do you no good at all."
sentences.n: ما ... بنافعة: the redundant بـ on the predicate strengthens the denial, as in “not the least use”. The girl speaks to a man, hence له (“to him”) and the masculine -ka.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نُورُالدِّينِ فَأَنَا فِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ أَقُومُ وَأَرُوحُ لَهُمْ وَأَطْرُقُ أَبْوَا بِهِمْ لَعَلَّ أَنْ يَحْصُلَ لِي مِنْهُمْ شَيٌ فَأَجْعَلَهُ فِي يَدِي رَأْسَ مَالٍ وَأَتَاجَرَ فِيهِ وَأَتْرُكَ اللَّهْوَ وَاللَّعِبَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Nūru al-Dīni fa-anā fī hādhihi al-sāʿati aqūmu wa-arūḥu lahum wa-aṭruqu abwā bihim laʿalla an yaḥṣula lī minhum shayʾun fa-ajʿalahu fī yadī raʾsa mālin wa-atājara fīhi wa-atruka al-lahwa wa-al-laʿiba
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn said: So I, at this hour, I-rise and I-go to them and I-knock their doors; perhaps that there come-about for me from them a-thing, and I-make it in my hand a-head-of-wealth, and I-trade in it and I-leave the amusement and the play.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn said, "This very hour I shall rise and go to them and knock at their doors. Perhaps something will come to me from them, and I shall take it in hand as capital, trade with it, and give up idleness and sport."
sentences.n: أبوا بهم is the print's division of أبوابهم, “their doors”; it is kept as printed. After لعل أن يحصل the verbs فأجعله، وأتاجر، وأترك are read as subjunctives continuing the hope (“perhaps ... and I may ...”), as a Classical writer would have them. رأس مال, “head of wealth”, is capital.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ نَهَضَ مِنْ وَقْتِهِ وَسَاعَتِهِ وَلَا زَالَ سَائِرً احَتَّى أَقْبَلَ عَلَى الزُّقَاقِ الَّذِي فِيهِ أَصْحَابُهُ الْعَشَرَةُ وَكَانُوا كُلُّهُمْ سَاكِنِينَ فِي ذَلِكَ الزُّقَاقِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu nahaḍa min waqtihi wa-sāʿatihi wa-lā zāla sāʾiran ḥattā aqbala ʿalā al-zuqāqi alladhī fīhi aṣḥābuhu al-ʿasharatu wa-kānū kulluhum sākinīna fī dhālika al-zuqāqi
sentences.l: Then he, he rose from his time and his hour, and did not cease going until he came-up upon the lane in-which (were) his companions, the ten, and they were all dwelling in that lane.
sentences.i: Then he rose that very moment and went on without stopping until he came to the lane where his ten friends lived, all of them dwelling in that one lane.
sentences.n: In the print the tanwīn-alif of سائرا stands at the head of the next word, so one reads سائر احتى as sāʾiran ḥattā; it is kept as printed. ولا زال, “and he did not cease”, is the ordinary way to say “he kept on”.

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ إِلَى أَوَّلِ بَابٍ وَطَرَقَهُ فَخَرَجَتْ لَهُ جَارِيَةٌ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ مَنْ أَنْتَ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama ilā awwali bābin wa-ṭaraqahu fa-kharajat lahu jāriyatun wa-qālat lahu man anta
sentences.l: And he advanced to the first of doors and knocked it, and there came-out to him a girl, and she said to-him: Who (are) you?
sentences.i: He went up to the first door and knocked, and a slave-girl came out to him and said, "Who are you?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا قُولِي لِسَيِّدِكَ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ وَ اقِفٌ عَلَى الْبَابِ وَيَقُولُ لَكَ مَمْلُوكُكَ يُقَبِّلُ يَدَيْكَ وَمُنْتَظِرٌ فَضْلَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā qūlī li-sayyidika Nūru al-Dīni ʿAliyyun wa āqifun ʿalā al-bābi wa-yaqūlu laka mamlūkuka yuqabbilu yadayka wa-muntaẓirun faḍlaka
sentences.l: And he said to-her: Say to-your-master: Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī (is) standing at the door, and says to-you your slave: he kisses your hands and (is) awaiting your bounty.
sentences.i: He said to her, "Tell your master that Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī is standing at the door, and that your servant kisses your hands and waits upon your bounty."
sentences.n: و اقف is printed as two words (the wāw detached) and read wāqifun, “standing”. The message is a courtly formula: “your slave kisses your hands and awaits your favour”.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ وَأَعْلَمَتْ سَيِّدَهَا فَزَعَقَ عَلَيْهَا وَقَالَ لَهَا اِرْجِعِي وَقُولِي لَهُ مَاهُوَ هُنَا
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalati al-jāriyatu wa-aʿlamat sayyidahā fa-zaʿaqa ʿalayhā wa-qāla lahā irjiʿī wa-qūlī lahu mā huwa hunā
sentences.l: And the girl entered and informed her master, and he shouted at her and said to-her: Return, and say to-him: He-is-not here.
sentences.i: The girl went in and told her master, who shouted at her and said, "Go back and tell him I am not here."
sentences.n: ماهو هنا, “he is not here”, uses ما with a pronoun subject and no verb, as colloquial Arabic does; the print writes ماهو as one word. The master speaks of himself in the third person, “he is not here”, as one does in sending away a caller.

sentences.t: فَرَجَعَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ إِلَى نُورِالدِّينِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي إِنَّ سَيِّدِي مَاهُوَ هُنَا
sentences.tr: fa-rajaʿati al-jāriyatu ilā Nūri al-Dīni wa-qālat lahu yā sayyidī inna sayyidī mā huwa hunā
sentences.l: And the girl returned to Nūr al-Dīn and said to-him: O my master, indeed my master, he-is-not here.
sentences.i: The girl came back to Nūr al-Dīn and said, "My lord, my master is not here."

sentences.t: فَتَوَجَّهَ نُورُالدِّينِ وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ إِنْ كَانَ هَذَا وَلَدَزِنًا وَأَنْكَرَ نَفْسَهُ فَخَيْرُهُ مَاهُوَ وَلَدَزِنًا
sentences.tr: fa-tawajjaha Nūru al-Dīni wa-qāla fī nafsihi in kāna hādhā waladazinan wa-ankara nafsahu fa-khayruhu mā huwa waladazinan
sentences.l: So Nūr al-Dīn turned away and said in himself: If this one is a son-of-fornication and disowned himself — then his-best (?) he is not a son-of-fornication.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn turned away and said to himself, "If this one is a bastard to deny himself, another of them surely is not."
sentences.n: فخيره is printed so, with خ, and is vocalised as it stands (“his good”), but the sense wants فغيره, “then another than he”, a single dotted letter away; the translation follows that sense. ولدزنا is walad zinā, “son of fornication”, run together as one word; زنا takes tanwīn here (zinan) as the genitive term of the construct.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ تَقَدَّمَ إِلَى بَابِ الثَّانِي وَقَالَ كَمَا قَالَ أَوَّلًا فَأَنْكَرَ نَفْسَهُ الْآخَرُ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ شِـــعْـــرٌ
sentences.tr: thumma taqaddama ilā bābi al-thānī wa-qāla kamā qāla awwalan fa-ankara nafsahu al-ākharu fa-ʿinda dhālika anshada yaqūlu shiʿrun
sentences.l: Then he advanced to the door the-second and said as he had said first, and the other disowned himself; and at that he recited, saying: Verse.
sentences.i: Then he went up to the second door and spoke as he had spoken before, and the other too denied himself. Thereupon he recited:
sentences.n: باب الثاني, “the door the second”, puts the article on the adjective though the noun has none; this is a common Middle Arabic way of saying “the second door”. The word شعر, “verse”, is the printer's heading for the poem that follows, stretched out to fill the line.

sentences.t: ذَهَبَ الَّذِينَ اِذَا وَقَفْتَ بِبَابِهِمْ * مَنُّوا عَلَيْكَ بِاَنْعُمٍ وَشِوَاءِ
sentences.tr: dhahaba alladhīna idhā waqafta bi-bābihim * mannū ʿalayka bi-anʿumin wa-shiwāʾi
sentences.l: Gone (are) those-who, when you stood at-their-door * they-favoured upon-you with-bounties and-roast-meat.
sentences.i: Gone are those who, when you stood at their door, * loaded you with favours and roast meat.
sentences.n: One line of verse, printed with its vowels; the pointing is kept exactly as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ قَٰلَ وَاللَّهِ لَا بُدَّأَنْ أَعْتِنُهُمْ كُلَّهُمْ لَعَلَّ يَكُونُ فِيهِمْ وَاحِدٌ يَقُومُ مَقَامَ الْجَمِيعِ لِلدَّارِ عَلَى الْعَشَرَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi qāla wa-Allāhi lā budda an aʿtinuhum kullahum laʿalla yakūnu fīhim wāḥidun yaqūmu maqāma al-jamīʿi li-al-dāri ʿalā al-ʿasharati
sentences.l: And when he finished from his verse, he said: By-God, there-is-no-escaping that I try-them (?), all-of-them; perhaps there-is among-them one (who) stands (in the) place of the whole, for the house, upon the ten.
sentences.i: When he had finished his verse he said, "By God, I must try every one of them; perhaps there is one among them who will stand in the place of the whole company, for the household's sake, instead of the ten."
sentences.n: قل is printed for قال and carries the dagger alif. اعتنهم is obscure: the letters as printed do not make a known verb, and I read it by sense as “I put them to the test”; it may be a transposition for أعنتهم (aʿnatahum, “I put them to trouble, I try them”, Lane) or for امتحنهم. لعل يكون has the indicative with no أن after لعل, as Middle Arabic often does. للدار على العشرة, “for the house, upon the ten”, is hard; I take it as “for the household's sake, in place of the ten”. Read it as uncertain.

sentences.t: فَمَا مِنْهُمْ مَنْ فَتَحَ الْبَابَ وَلَا رَاهُ نَفْسَهُ وَلَاكَسَرَ فِي وَجْهِهِ رَغِيفًا فَأَنْشَدَ يَقُـــــــولُ
sentences.tr: fa-mā minhum man fataḥa al-bāba wa-lā rāhu nafsahu wa-lākasara fī wajhihi raghīfan fa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: And not among-them (was one) who opened the door, nor (showed) him his-self, nor broke in his face a loaf; and he recited, saying:
sentences.i: Not one of them opened the door, or showed his face, or broke a loaf of bread before him; so he recited:
sentences.n: راه نفسه is printed so; the sense is أراه نفسه, “showed him himself”, with the initial alif of the verb missing from the print. It is vocalised as printed (rāhu) and translated by the sense. “To break bread in someone's face” is to offer him a meal.

sentences.t:
اَلْمَرْأُ فِي زَمَنِ الْاِقْبَالِ كَالشَّجَرَةْ * وَالنَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهَا مَادَامَتْ لِلثَّمَرَةْ
حَتَّى اِذَا رَاحَ عَنْهَا حِمْلُهَا رَحَلُوا * وَخَفُّوهَا تُقَاسِي الْحَرَّ وَالْغَبَرَةْ
تَبًّا لِاَبْنَاءِ هَذَا الدَّهْرِ كُلِّهِــمِ * حَتَّى وَلَا وَاحِدٌ يَصْفُو مِنَ الْعَشَرَةْ
sentences.tr:
al-marʾu fī zamani al-iqbāli ka-al-shajarah * wa-al-nāsu min ḥawlihā mā dāmat li-al-thamarah
ḥattā idhā rāḥa ʿanhā ḥimluhā raḥalū * wa-khaffūhā tuqāsī al-ḥarra wa-al-ghabarah
tabban li-abnāʾi hādhā al-dahri kullihimi * ḥattā wa-lā wāḥidun yaṣfū mina al-ʿasharah
sentences.n: Three lines of verse, printed with their vowels; the pointing is kept as printed. وخفوها is printed so (the verb of خفّ, “be light”); it is obscure, and I take it as for وخلّفوها, “and they left it behind”, which the sense requires. مادامت للثمرة, “as long as it is for the fruit”, means “as long as it has fruit”.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ رَجَعَ إِلَى جَارِيَتِهِ وَقَدْ تَزَايَدَ هَمُّهُ فَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَاسَيِّدِي أَنَا مَا قُلْتُ لَكَ إِنَّهُمْ لَا يَنْفَعُونَكَ بِنَافِعَةٍ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu rajaʿa ilā jāriyatihi wa-qad tazāyada hammuhu fa-qālat lahu yā sayyidī anā mā qultu laka innahum lā yanfaʿūnaka bi-nāfiʿatin
sentences.l: Then he, he returned to his girl, his worry having increased, and she said to-him: O my master, I — did-I-not say to-you that-they will-not benefit-you with a benefiting?
sentences.i: Then he went back to his slave-girl, his sorrow grown greater, and she said, "My master, did I not tell you that they would do you no good?"
sentences.n: أنا ما قلت لك is a rhetorical “did I not tell you?”, the negative statement being offered as a question.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ مَا فِيهِمْ مَنْ أَرَانِي وَجْهَهُ وَلَا فِيهِمْ أَحَدٌ يَعْرِفُ بِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-Allāhi mā fīhim man arānī wajhahu wa-lā fīhim aḥadun yaʿrifu bī
sentences.l: And he said: By-God, not among-them (is one) who showed-me his-face, and not among-them anyone (who) knows of-me.
sentences.i: He said, "By God, there is not one of them who would show me his face, nor one who will own that he knows me."
sentences.n: يعرف بي: ʿarafa takes its object with بـ here in the sense of “take notice of, acknowledge”; the direct object is the Classical construction.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا سَيِّدِي بِعْ مِنْ أَثَاثِ الْبَيْتِ وَآنِيَتِهِ إِلَى أَنْ يُدَبِّرَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى وَأَنْفِقْ أَوَّلًا بِأَوَّلٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu yā sayyidī biʿ min athāthi al-bayti wa-āniyatihi ilā an yudabbira Allāhu taʿālā wa-anfiq awwalan bi-awwalin
